tips.title: A Guide to Getting Started
paragraphs: Fertility is a personal aspect of health, and every individual or couple may have different questions, circumstances, and goals. Understanding your options can help you have informed conversations with a qualified healthcare professional.
A good starting point is to discuss your medical history, concerns, and expectations with your healthcare provider. They can help determine which assessments, if any, may be appropriate for you.

tips.title: Lifestyle and reproductive health
paragraphs: General health habits can support overall well-being. Eating a varied, balanced diet, getting adequate rest, avoiding tobacco, and discussing medications or supplements with a clinician can all be useful topics to consider.
Lifestyle changes cannot guarantee conception. Your age, medical history, and other factors may influence fertility, so personalized guidance is important.

tips.title: Understanding treatment options
paragraphs: Depending on your circumstances, a specialist may discuss diagnostic testing, medication, intrauterine insemination (IUI), in vitro fertilization (IVF), or other approaches. Not every option is appropriate for every person.

detail.intro: A medical emergency rarely gives notice, and the cost of treatment can strain even careful savings. Health insurance lets you focus on recovery rather than on how the bills will be paid.

sections.title: 1. Manage Rising
sections.text: Hospital stays, surgeries, and diagnostic tests become more expensive every year. A health plan covers a large share of these costs so that one illness does not undo years of saving.

sections.title: 2. Get Care
sections.text: Many plans offer cashless treatment at network hospitals, which means you can be admitted and treated without arranging a large payment first. Check the hospital list near your home before you buy.

sections.title: 3. Cover the
sections.text: A family floater plan protects your spouse, children, and sometimes parents under a single sum insured. Review the waiting periods and exclusions so you know exactly what is covered and from when.

tip.title: Tip: Read the Waiting Periods
tip.text: Most policies apply a waiting period to pre-existing conditions and certain treatments. Knowing these before you buy helps you avoid surprises at claim time.

detail.imageAlt: Travellers watching a plane from an airport terminal
detail.intro: A trip takes weeks of planning, but a missed flight, a lost bag, or a sudden illness abroad can change it in minutes. Travel insurance is a small addition to your budget that keeps those setbacks from becoming expensive problems.

sections.title: 1. Medical Help
sections.text: Treatment in another country can be costly and hard to arrange. Travel cover pays for emergency medical care and, where needed, evacuation, so you are not left negotiating bills in an unfamiliar place.

sections.title: 2. Delays and
sections.text: If your trip is cancelled or cut short for a covered reason, the policy can reimburse non-refundable bookings. Many plans also compensate for long flight delays and missed connections.

sections.title: 3. Lost Baggage and
sections.text: Losing your luggage or passport is stressful enough without the cost of replacing them. Cover for baggage and travel documents helps you get essentials quickly and continue your journey.

tip.title: Tip: Buy When You Book
tip.text: Purchasing cover at the time you book your trip means cancellation benefits apply from day one, not just from the day you depart.

posts.title: Home Insurance: Protect What Matters Most
posts.text: See how home insurance shields your house and belongings from fire, theft, and natural calamities.

detail.intro: Your home is likely the most valuable thing you own, and everything inside it took years to build up. Home insurance protects both the structure and your belongings against events you cannot control.

sections.title: 1. Cover the
sections.text: Fire, storms, floods, and other calamities can cause damage that is expensive to repair. Structure cover pays towards rebuilding or restoring your home so you are not starting again from nothing.

sections.title: 2. Protect Your
sections.text: Furniture, appliances, electronics, and valuables can be insured against theft and damage. Keep a simple list of what you own and its approximate value to make any claim faster.

sections.title: 3. Choose the Right
sections.text: Insure the structure for what it would cost to rebuild, not its market price, and review the amount whenever you renovate. Being under-insured can reduce what you receive at claim time.

tip.title: Tip: Renters Need Cover Too
tip.text: If you rent, you can still insure your belongings. Contents-only cover is usually inexpensive and protects everything you have brought into the home.

posts.title: Motor Insurance: Drive with Complete Confidence
posts.text: Understand third-party and comprehensive cover, and how the right add-ons keep you protected on every journey.

detail.imageAlt: Car driving along a winding road at sunset
detail.intro: Every drive carries some risk, however careful you are. Motor insurance protects you from the cost of accidents, theft, and damage, and keeps you on the right side of the law.

sections.title: 1. Third-Party or
sections.text: Third-party cover pays for injury or damage you cause to others and is the legal minimum in many places. Comprehensive cover adds protection for your own vehicle against accidents, theft, fire, and natural events.

sections.title: 2. Add-Ons That
sections.text: Zero depreciation, roadside assistance, and engine protection can make a real difference when you claim. Choose add-ons based on your car’s age, where you drive, and how much you would want to pay out of pocket.

sections.title: 3. Keep Your
sections.text: Each claim-free year usually earns a discount on your next premium. Renew on time and think twice before claiming for very small repairs, so the bonus keeps building.

tip.title: Tip: Renew Before Expiry
tip.text: A lapsed policy can mean losing your no-claim bonus and driving uninsured. Set a reminder a few weeks before your renewal date.

posts.title: Business Insurance: Safeguard What You’ve Built
posts.text: Learn how the right cover protects your assets, your people, and your income when something goes wrong.

detail.imageAlt: Business owner meeting with an insurance advisor
detail.intro: A business takes years to build and can be set back by a single unexpected event. Business insurance helps you absorb the shock and keep trading while you recover.

sections.title: 1. Protect Your
sections.text: Premises, equipment, and stock are the foundation of your operations. Property cover helps you repair or replace them after fire, theft, or damage so work can resume sooner.

sections.title: 2. Cover Your
sections.text: A customer injury, a faulty product, or a professional error can lead to claims against you. Liability cover pays for legal costs and compensation that could otherwise threaten the business.

sections.title: 3. Keep Income
sections.text: If you have to close temporarily, business interruption cover can replace lost income and help with fixed costs such as rent and salaries until you are back on your feet.

tip.title: Tip: Review Cover as You Grow
tip.text: New staff, new premises, or new services all change your risks. Revisit your policy every year so your cover grows with the business.

InsuranceFaqPage1.intro: Answers to common questions about choosing insurance, claims, tax benefits, and policy add-ons.

items.question: How do I choose the best insurance plan for my family?
items.answer: Our certified advisors assess your family size, current medical history, liabilities, and long-term financial goals to recommend the most cost-effective and comprehensive coverage.

items.question: How does Surevia help during insurance claim settlements?
items.answer: We provide dedicated end-to-end claim assistance: from filing initial paperwork and coordinating directly with hospital/insurer TPA desks to ensuring full settlement disbursement without delays.

items.question: Are tax benefits available under Indian insurance laws?
items.answer: Yes, premiums paid towards life insurance qualify for deductions under Section 80C, while health insurance premiums qualify under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act.

items.question: Can I customize policy add-ons and riders?
items.answer: Absolutely. You can enhance your coverage with riders like Critical Illness, Accidental Disability, Zero Depreciation, and Maternity Coverage according to your needs.

faqSection.title: Frequently Asked
faqSection.description: Find answers to common questions about fertility, IVF treatments, appointments, and the care we provide. We are here to make your journey easier to understand.

items.question: What is IVF and how does the process work?
items.answer: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) is a fertility treatment in which eggs and sperm are combined in a laboratory. If fertilization occurs, an embryo may be transferred to the uterus. Your fertility specialist will explain each stage and help determine whether IVF is appropriate for you.

items.question: Who may benefit from fertility treatment?
items.answer: Fertility treatment may be considered for people experiencing difficulties conceiving or those with certain reproductive health conditions. A consultation and appropriate medical assessment help determine the most suitable options.

items.question: How long does an IVF treatment cycle take?
items.answer: The timeline varies depending on your medical history, treatment protocol, and individual response. A treatment cycle may take several weeks, and your doctor will provide a personalized timeline after your assessment.

items.question: Is IVF treatment painful?
items.answer: Experiences differ from person to person. Some stages may involve mild discomfort, and your medical team can explain what to expect and discuss ways to manage discomfort throughout treatment.

items.question: What tests are required before starting IVF?
items.answer: Your doctor may recommend blood tests, ultrasound scans, and other assessments based on your medical history. Testing helps your specialist understand your reproductive health and plan appropriate care.

items.question: What factors affect the cost of IVF treatment?
items.answer: The overall cost depends on the treatment plan, investigations, medications, procedures, and any additional services required. Our team can explain the expected costs before treatment begins.

items.question: Can I continue my normal routine during treatment?
items.answer: Many everyday activities can continue during parts of treatment, but recommendations may change depending on the treatment stage. Follow the guidance provided by your fertility specialist.

items.question: How can I book an appointment?
items.answer: You can contact our care team through the appointment form, phone, or contact page. Our team will help arrange a consultation at a convenient time.
